newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lauda Air sees 20 pct 96-97 German passenger growth.
newsitem.headline: Lauda Air sees 20 pct 96-97 German passenger growth.

text.p: Lauda Air said it expected 20 percent growth to 120,000 passengers from Germany in 1996-97.
The Austrian carrier's general manager for Germany, Michael Svedek, said sales revenue was likely to rise 30 percent to 65 million marks in the September 1996-August 1997 fiscal year.
"The Germany routes have load factors of more than 60 percent and we are very happy with them financially," he told Reuters in an interview.
"Duesseldorf and Munich are the most profitable routes we have and Frankfurt makes a small profit," he added.
Sales to Australia, Hong Kong and Miami were currently strong and Thailand had picked up after a weak 1996, Svedek said.
Germany was the second-largest market for Lauda Air after Austria, he added.
Lauda Air flies from Vienna and Salzburg to Frankfurt, Duesseldorf, Munich and Berlin.
